source.name: AISafety.com field map
source.note: Names, short names, categories, size marks and descriptions are from the map’s own records and are reused under its licence.

entries.name: PauseAI
entries.desc: Campaign group aiming to convince governments to pause AI development – through public outreach, engaging with decision-makers, and organizing protests.

entries.name: Future of Life Institute (FLI)
entries.desc: Steering transformative technology towards benefitting life and away from extreme large-scale risks through outreach, policy advocacy, grantmaking, and event organization.

entries.name: Astral Codex Ten (ACX)
entries.desc: Blog by Scott Alexander covering many topics, including reasoning, science, ethics, economics, politics, and AI. Often posts book summaries and commentary on AI safety.

entries.name: Don't Worry about the Vase
entries.desc: Blog by Zvi Mowshowitz on various topics, including AI, offering detailed analysis, personal insights, and a rationalist perspective. Posts very frequently.

entries.name: Anthropic
entries.desc: Capabilities company focusing on LLM alignment, particularly interpretability. Featuring Chris Olah, Jack Clark, and Dario Amodei. Created Claude.

entries.name: Google DeepMind
entries.desc: London-based capabilities company with a strong safety team, led by Demis Hassabis. Created AlphaGo, AlphaFold, and Gemini.

entries.name: OpenAI
entries.desc: Capabilities company that created ChatGPT, led by Sam Altman. Throughout 2024, roughly half of then-employed AI safety researchers left the company.

entries.name: How to pursue a career in technical AI alignment
entries.desc: A guide written for people who are familiar with the arguments for the importance of AI alignment and are considering pursuing a career working on it.

entries.name: Successif
entries.desc: Helping professionals transition to high-impact work by performing market research on impactful jobs and providing career mentoring, opportunity matching, and professional training.

entries.name: Arcadia Impact
entries.desc: Runs various projects aimed at education, skill development, and creating pathways into impactful careers. Recently also launched a research arm.

entries.name: Alignment Research Center (ARC)
entries.desc: Research organization led by Paul Christiano trying to understand how to formalize mechanistic explanations of neural network behavior.

entries.name: Resolution
entries.desc: Nonprofit founded by Geoffrey Irving, former Chief Scientist of UK AISI, using theory plus automation to pursue higher-confidence approaches to aligning superintelligent AI.

entries.name: AE Studio
entries.desc: Large team taking a 'Neglected Approaches' approach to alignment, tackling the problem from multiple, often overlooked angles in both technical and policy domains.

entries.name: AI Alignment Forum
entries.desc: Hub for researchers to discuss all ideas related to AI safety. Discussion ranges from technical models of agency to the strategic landscape, and everything in between.

entries.name: Model Evaluation & Threat Research (METR)
entries.desc: Researching, developing, and running evaluations of AI capabilities, including broad autonomous capabilities and the ability of AI systems to conduct AI R&D.

entries.name: Redwood Research
entries.desc: Nonprofit researching AI control and alignment faking. Also consults governments and AI companies on AI safety practices.

entries.name: Center for AI Safety (CAIS)
entries.desc: Conducting safety research, building the field of AI safety researchers, and advocating for safety standards.

entries.name: AI Safety Tactical Opportunities Fund (AISTOF)
entries.desc: Pooled multi-donor fund structured to be fast and rapidly capture emerging opportunities. Managed by JueYan Zhang.

entries.name: Coefficient Giving (CG)
entries.desc: The largest funder in the existential risk space, backed primarily by Dustin Moskovitz and Cari Tuna. Previously called Open Philanthropy.

entries.name: grantmaking.ai
entries.desc: Public database of AI safety projects seeking funding, with community evaluations to help donors coordinate. Currently running a $1M grant round.

entries.name: Lightcone Commons
entries.desc: New grantmaking platform coordinating large-scale philanthropy – funders split grant costs proportionally and evaluators vet applications in quarterly funding rounds.

entries.name: Longview Philanthropy
entries.desc: Devises and executes bespoke giving strategies for major donors, working with them at all stages of their giving journey.

entries.name: Manifund
entries.desc: Marketplace for funding new charities, including in AI safety. Users can find impactful projects, buy impact certificates, and weigh in on what gets funded.

entries.name: Survival and Flourishing Fund (SFF)
entries.desc: The second largest funder in AI safety, using an algorithm and meeting procedure called the S-process to allocate grants.

entries.name: Transformative AI Fund (TAIF)
entries.desc: Funds new projects addressing transformative AI, with grants typically $10k-$150k. Run by Effective Altruism Funds. Replaced the Long-Term Future Fund (LTFF).

entries.name: UK AI Security Institute (UK AISI)
entries.desc: UK government organization conducting research and building infrastructure to test the safety of advanced AI and measure its impacts. Also working to shape global policy.

entries.name: Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI)
entries.desc: The original AI safety technical research organization, co-founded by Eliezer Yudkowsky. Now focusing on policy and public outreach.

entries.name: Import AI
entries.desc: Weekly updates on the latest developments in AI research (including governance) written by Jack Clark, co-founder of Anthropic.

entries.name: Transformer
entries.desc: Aiming to help decision-makers understand what’s happening in AI and why it matters – through news roundups, explainers, features, and opinion pieces.

entries.name: 80,000 Hours Podcast
entries.desc: In-depth conversations about the world’s most pressing problems – including AI safety – and what you can do to help solve them.

entries.name: Alignment Ecosystem Development (AED)
entries.desc: Building and maintaining key online resources for the AI safety community, including AISafety.com and AISafety.info. Volunteers welcome.

entries.name: Centre for Enabling EA Learning & Research (CEEALAR aka EA Hotel)
entries.desc: Residential incubator for effective altruist researchers, founders, and career transitioners, with a strong focus on AI safety.

entries.name: EquiStamp
entries.desc: Engineering company providing evaluation implementation, data annotation, and project operations so AI safety researchers can focus on research.

entries.name: Lightcone Infrastructure
entries.desc: Nonprofit maintaining LessWrong, the Alignment Forum, Lighthaven, and Lightcone Commons.

entries.name: Apart Research
entries.desc: Accelerates AI safety research through mentorship, collaborations, and open-to-all research sprints.

entries.name: AISafety.com
entries.desc: Hub for key resources for the AI safety community, including directories of courses, jobs, upcoming events and training programs etc. – and this map!

entries.name: Effective Altruism Forum
entries.desc: Forum on doing good as effectively as possible, including AI safety. Also has a podcast featuring text-to-speech narrations of top posts.

entries.name: LessWrong
entries.desc: Online forum dedicated to improving human reasoning, containing a lot of AI safety content. Also has a podcast featuring text-to-speech narrations of top posts.

entries.name: AISafety.info
entries.desc: Accessible guide to AI safety for those new to the space, in the form of a comprehensive FAQ and AI safety chatbot. Project of Rob Miles.

entries.name: Anthropic Fellows Program
entries.desc: Provides funding, compute, and mentorship for technical talent entering empirical AI safety research. Fellows work on scalable oversight, interpretability, and AI control.

entries.name: BlueDot Impact
entries.desc: Runs the standard introductory courses for people new to AI safety. Two main streams: Technical AI Safety and Frontier AI Governance.

entries.name: Dovetail Research Fellowship
entries.desc: Agent foundations research program. Participants work on pure-math problems drawing on probability theory, information theory, and dynamical systems.

entries.name: Iliad Fellowship
entries.desc: Supports mentored research in applied mathematics for alignment – aimed at PhD, postdoctoral, and similarly experienced researchers in math, physics, and related fields.

entries.name: Iliad Intensive
entries.desc: Introduction to technical alignment for people with strong math backgrounds. Modules span deep learning theory, interpretability, agent foundations, and safety guarantees.

entries.name: Lens Academy
entries.desc: Online courses guiding people from first understanding why superintelligent AI could be catastrophic,  to discovering what they can do about it.

entries.name: Machine Alignment, Transparency, and Security (MATS)
entries.desc: Research program connecting talented scholars with top mentors in AI safety. Involves 12 weeks onsite mentored research and, if selected, 6–12 months extended research.

entries.name: PIBBSS Fellowship
entries.desc: 3-month interdisciplinary program run by Princint connecting researchers from diverse fields with AI safety mentors, in order to help them transition their career to AI safety.

entries.name: Rational Animations
entries.desc: Animated videos aiming to foster good thinking, promote altruistic causes, and help ensure humanity's future goes well – particularly regarding AI safety.

entries.name: Robert Miles
entries.desc: The most popular AI safety education channel, explaining technical alignment concepts to general audiences through accessible explainer videos.

entries.name: Existential Risk Observatory (ERO)
entries.desc: Informing the public debate on existential risks, on the basis that awareness is the first step towards reducing those risks.

entries.name: AI Frontiers
entries.desc: Platform from the Center for AI Safety (CAIS) posting articles written by experts from a wide range of fields discussing the impacts of AI.

entries.name: AI Safety Takes
entries.desc: Blog by AI safety researcher Daniel Paleka curating and succinctly analyzing the latest research and news in AI safety. Posts about every two months.

entries.name: Planned Obsolescence
entries.desc: Substack by Ajeya Cotra, researcher at METR, covering AI capabilities forecasting, AI agent benchmarks, timelines for automating AI R&D, and implications for AI safety.

entries.name: AISafety.com: Media channels
entries.desc: The AI safety space is changing rapidly. This directory of key information sources can help you keep up to date with the latest developments.

entries.name: SpaceXAI
entries.desc: Capabilities lab led by Elon Musk with the mission of advancing our collective understanding of the universe. Created Grok.

entries.name: Astera Neuro-AI
entries.desc: Astera Institute's research program pursuing neuroscience-informed AGI, with efforts in neuroscience, AI, and AI safety.

entries.name: Safe Superintelligence Inc. (SSI)
entries.desc: Research lab founded by Ilya Sutskever, comprised of a small team of engineers and researchers working towards building a safe superintelligence.

entries.name: 80,000 Hours Job Board
entries.desc: Curated list of job posts around the world tackling pressing problems, including AI safety. Also has a newsletter.

entries.name: 80,000 Hours Problem Profile
entries.desc: Regularly-updated article with motivation and advice around pursuing a career in AI safety.

entries.name: AI Safety Quest
entries.desc: Grassroots volunteer organization helping people navigate the AI safety ecosystem, connect with like-minded people, and find projects that are a good fit for their skills.

entries.name: AISafety.com: Advisors
entries.desc: Directory of advisors offering free guidance calls to help you discover how best to contribute to AI safety, tailored to your skills and interests.

entries.name: Alignment of Complex Systems Research Group (ACS)
entries.desc: Studying questions about multi-agent systems composed of humans and advanced AI. Based at Charles University, Prague.

entries.name: Arbital
entries.desc: Wiki on AI alignment theory, mostly written by Eliezer Yudkowsky. Includes foundational concepts, open problems, and proposed solutions.

entries.name: Center for Human-Compatible AI (CHAI)
entries.desc: Developing the conceptual and technical wherewithal to reorient the general thrust of AI research towards provably beneficial systems. Led by Stuart Russell at UC Berkeley.

entries.name: John Wentworth
entries.desc: Independent alignment researcher working on selection theorems, abstraction, and agency.

entries.name: Orthogonal
entries.desc: Formal alignment organization led by Tamsin Leake, focused on agent foundations. Also has a public Discord server.

entries.name: Association for Long Term Existence and Resilience (ALTER)
entries.desc: Israeli academic research and advocacy nonprofit working to investigate, demonstrate, and foster useful ways to safeguard and improve the future of humanity.

entries.name: Modeling Cooperation
entries.desc: Conducts research and builds software helping improve cooperation in competition for the development of transformative AI.

entries.name: Center on Long-Term Risk (CLR)
entries.desc: Research, grants, and community-building around AI safety, focused on conflict scenarios as well as technical and philosophical aspects of cooperation.

entries.name: Iliad
entries.desc: Research and field-building org that incubates technical research bets, runs a training program, hosts conferences and a fellowship, and has launched an alignment journal.

entries.name: Principles of Intelligence (Princint)
entries.desc: Helps build scientific foundations for AI safety through interdisciplinary research programs, the PIBBSS Fellowship, and internal research.

entries.name: LawZero
entries.desc: Advancing research and developing technical solutions for safe-by-design AI systems based on Scientist AI, a research direction led by Yoshua Bengio.

entries.name: Meaning Alignment Institute (MAI)
entries.desc: Researching how to align AI, markets, and democracies with what people value – from theory to practice.

entries.name: Ought
entries.desc: Product-driven research lab developing mechanisms for delegating high-quality reasoning to ML systems. Built Elicit, an AI assistant for researchers and academics.

entries.name: TruthfulAI
entries.desc: Nonprofit led by Owain Evans, researching situational awareness, deception, and hidden reasoning in LLMs.

entries.name: EleutherAI
entries.desc: Open-source research lab focused on interpretability and alignment. Operates primarily through a public Discord server, where research is discussed and projects are coordinated.

entries.name: Apollo Research
entries.desc: Researches the science of scheming and its mitigations, conducts pre-deployment evals, supports technical governance, and builds tools to secure agents.

entries.name: Cambridge Programme on AI Science & Policy (CASP)
entries.desc: University of Cambridge research group, part of the Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence (CFI). Advances knowledge for high-stakes decisions on frontier AI.

entries.name: FAR.AI
entries.desc: Conducting research, hosting events, and running programs – including the FAR.Lab coworking space.

entries.name: AI Futures Project (AIFP)
entries.desc: Small research group forecasting the future of AI. Created 'AI 2027', a detailed forecast scenario projecting the development of artificial superintelligence.

entries.name: Forecasting Research Institute (FRI)
entries.desc: Advancing the science of forecasting for the public good by working with policymakers and nonprofits to design practical forecasting tools, and test them in large experiments.

entries.name: Manifold Markets
entries.desc: Prediction market platform covering many topics, using play money called mana. Features markets on AI and AI safety.

entries.name: Metaculus
entries.desc: Well-calibrated forecasting platform covering a wide range of topics, including AI and AI safety.

entries.name: Quantified Uncertainty Research Institute (QURI)
entries.desc: Conducted research and built software in order to advance forecasting and epistemics to improve the long-term future of humanity. Now in maintenance mode.

entries.name: Transformative Futures Institute (TFI)
entries.desc: Research nonprofit utilizing foresight to mitigate societal-scale risks from advanced AI and other potential global catastrophic risks.

entries.name: Epoch AI
entries.desc: Research institute examining the driving forces behind AI and forecasting its economic and societal impact.

entries.name: Advanced Research + Invention Agency (ARIA)
entries.desc: UK government R&D funding agency aiming to unlock scientific and technological breakthroughs that benefit everyone. Similar to DARPA in the US.

entries.name: AI Risk Mitigation (ARM) Fund
entries.desc: Aiming to reduce catastrophic risks from advanced AI through grants towards technical research, policy, and training programs for new researchers.

entries.name: AISafety.com: Funding
entries.desc: Comprehensive directory of sources of financial support for AI safety projects.

entries.name: Astralis Foundation
entries.desc: Funding initiative with $25M annual giving, backing people and ideas with the funding, strategic guidance, and networks they need to steer transformative AI toward beneficial outcomes.

entries.name: Center on Long-Term Risk (CLR): Fund
entries.desc: Supports projects and individuals aiming to address worst-case suffering risks from the development and deployment of advanced AI systems.

entries.name: Cooperative AI Foundation (CAIF)
entries.desc: Charity foundation backed by a large philanthropic commitment supporting research into improving cooperative intelligence of advanced AI.

entries.name: EA Infrastructure Fund (EAIF)
entries.desc: Aims to increase the impact of effective altruism projects (including AI safety) by increasing their access to talent, capital, and knowledge. Run by Effective Altruism Funds.

entries.name: Ergo Impact
entries.desc: Helping philanthropists find, fund, and scale the most promising people and solutions to the world’s most pressing problems.

entries.name: Foresight Institute: Funding
entries.desc: Foresight's 'AI for Science & Safety Nodes' program offers funding, a community hub, and local compute in either San Francisco or Berlin.

entries.name: Founders Pledge
entries.desc: Helping entrepreneurs direct their charitable giving where it will do the most good by researching the world’s biggest problems and identifying the most effective solutions.

entries.name: Future of Life Foundation (FLF)
entries.desc: FLI-affiliated accelerator aiming to steer transformative technology towards benefiting life and away from extreme large-scale risks by launching 3–5 organizations per year

entries.name: Giving What We Can (GWWC)
entries.desc: Community of donors who have pledged to donate a significant portion of their income to highly effective charities, including those in AI safety.

entries.name: Science of Trustworthy AI
entries.desc: Funder housing the science-focused philanthropic efforts of Eric and Wendy Schmidt, moving funding towards AI safety via its AI institute.

entries.name: The Navigation Fund
entries.desc: Jed McCaleb's fund, making grants to organizations and projects in various cause areas – including AI safety.

entries.name: AI Alignment Foundation (AIAF)
entries.desc: Funds alignment researchers with ideas they can't pursue within their current institutional funding and experts from other fields whose perspectives could produce breakthroughs.

entries.name: AI Policy Institute (AIPI)
entries.desc: Channeling public concern around AI into effective regulation through engaging with policymakers, media, and the public.

entries.name: Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET)
entries.desc: Georgetown University think tank providing decision-makers with data-driven analysis on the security implications of emerging technologies.

entries.name: Centre for Future Generations (CFG)
entries.desc: Brussels think tank focused on helping governments anticipate and responsibly govern the societal impacts of rapid technological change.

entries.name: Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI)
entries.desc: AI governance research group at Oxford, producing research tailored towards decision-makers and running career development programs.

entries.name: European AI Office
entries.desc: Established within the European Commission as the centre of AI expertise in the EU, playing a key role in implementing the AI Act.

entries.name: Institute for Law & AI (LawAI)
entries.desc: Think tank researching and advising on the legal challenges posed by AI, premised on the idea that sound legal analysis will promote security, welfare, and the rule of law.

entries.name: The Future Society (TFS)
entries.desc: Drawing on their analyses and networks to provide global decision-makers with pragmatic guidance on navigating technological, catastrophic, and political risks from AI.

entries.name: ControlAI
entries.desc: Nonprofit fighting to keep humanity in control of AI by conducting public outreach, helping people contact their representatives, and briefing policymakers.

entries.name: SaferAI
entries.desc: French nonprofit developing quantitative risk models, evaluating company practices, and leading standards development that shapes AI regulation.

entries.name: Centre pour la Sécurité de l'IA (CeSIA)
entries.desc: French nonprofit working on research and education, public policy analysis, and strategic recommendations.

entries.name: AI Safety Events & Training
entries.desc: Weekly newsletter listing newly-announced AI safety events and training programs, both online and in-person.

entries.name: AI Safety Funding
entries.desc: Newsletter listing newly announced funding opportunities for individuals and organizations working to reduce AI existential risk.

entries.name: AI Safety Newsletter
entries.desc: Newsletter published every few weeks discussing recent developments in AI and AI safety. No technical background required.

entries.name: AI StopWatch
entries.desc: Newsroom experiment by comms analysts and writers at MIRI, posting daily updates and commentary on AI news.

entries.name: AI X-risk Research Podcast (AXRP)
entries.desc: Interviews with (mostly technical) AI safety researchers about their research, aiming to get a sense of why it was written and how it might reduce existential risk from AI.

entries.name: Future of Life Institute (FLI) Podcast
entries.desc: Interviews with existential risk researchers, policy experts, philosophers, and a range of other influential thinkers.

entries.name: The Cognitive Revolution
entries.desc: Weekly podcast where host Nathan Labenz interviews AI innovators and thinkers, discussing the transformative impact AI will likely have in the near future.

entries.name: Ashgro
entries.desc: Providing fiscal sponsorship to AI safety projects, saving them time and allowing them to access more funding.

entries.name: Berkeley Existential Risk Initiative (BERI)
entries.desc: Providing operational infrastructure and fiscal sponsorship to research groups working on existential risk, especially those based at a university.

entries.name: Catalyze Impact
entries.desc: Brings together co-founders, experts, and mission-oriented funders to accelerate founders from pre-idea to scaling an AI safety org.

entries.name: Constellation
entries.desc: Center for collaborative research in AI safety, supporting promising work through fellowships, an incubator, and hosting individuals and teams.

entries.name: European Network for AI Safety (ENAIS)
entries.desc: Community of researchers and policymakers from over 13 countries across Europe, united in their efforts to advance AI safety.

entries.name: Future Matters
entries.desc: Conducts research and provides strategy consulting services to clients trying to advance AI safety – and other causes – through policy, politics, coalitions, or social movements.

entries.name: London Initiative for Safe AI (LISA)
entries.desc: Coworking space hosting organizations (including BlueDot Impact, Apollo Research), acceleration programs (including MATS, ARENA), and independent researchers.

entries.name: Meridian
entries.desc: Coworking space and field-building nonprofit based in Cambridge, UK. Houses projects like CAISH and the ERA:AI Fellowship, as well as visiting AI safety researchers.

entries.name: AI Digest
entries.desc: Concise visual explainers of important trends in AI, grounded in concrete examples of what AI models can do right now.

entries.name: AI Plans
entries.desc: Searchable, peer-reviewed compendium of alignment plans, papers, and research directions. Also runs hackathons and produces courses and guides on AI safety.

entries.name: AI Watch
entries.desc: Database tracking people and organizations in the AI safety community, serving as a reference for positions, affiliations, and related data.

entries.name: The Guardrail
entries.desc: AI-powered platform that filters hundreds of arXiv papers daily, surfacing research relevant to AI safety. Features a weekly top 10 digest.

entries.name: Towards Superintelligence Alignment (TSA)
entries.desc: Companion site for a research manuscript proposing a framework for superintelligence alignment, with guided reading paths, a Lean formalization, experiments, and interactive demos.

entries.name: Centre for the Study of Existential Risk (CSER)
entries.desc: Interdisciplinary research center at the University of Cambridge dedicated to the study and mitigation of existential and global catastrophic risks.

entries.name: Global Partnership on AI (GPAI)
entries.desc: International initiative with 46 member countries working to implement human-centric, safe, secure, and trustworthy AI embodied in the principles of the OECD Recommendation on AI.

entries.name: Median Group
entries.desc: Research nonprofit working on models of past and future progress in AI, intelligence enhancement, and sociology related to existential risks.

entries.name: Partnership on AI (PAI)
entries.desc: Convening academic, civil society, industry, and media organizations to create solutions so that AI advances positive outcomes for people and society.

entries.name: Convergence Analysis
entries.desc: Building a foundational series of sociotechnical reports on key AI scenarios and governance recommendations, and conducting awareness campaigns.

entries.name: AI Impacts
entries.desc: Answering decision-relevant questions about the future of AI, including through research, a wiki, and expert surveys.

entries.name: Centre for Long-Term Resilience (CLTR)
entries.desc: Think tank aiming to transform global resilience to extreme risks by improving relevant governance, processes, and decision-making.

entries.name: AFFINE Network
entries.desc: Helps newcomers understand the core problems of superintelligence alignment through a seminar, research retreats, and a year-long fellowship.

entries.name: AI Safety Camp (AISC)
entries.desc: 3-month part-time online research program with mentorship, aimed at helping people who want to work on AI safety team up together on concrete projects.

entries.name: AISafety.com: Self-study
entries.desc: Comprehensive directory of AI safety curricula and reading lists for self-led learning at all levels.

entries.name: Alignment Research Engineer Accelerator (ARENA)
entries.desc: 4–5 week ML engineering upskilling program, focusing on alignment. Aims to provide people with the skills, community, and confidence to contribute directly to technical AI safety.

entries.name: Apart Fellowship
entries.desc: Turns hackathon projects into peer-reviewed publications. Fellows work in small teams with mentorship, compute, and travel support. Entry is by doing well in a research sprint.

entries.name: Astra Fellowship
entries.desc: Program at Constellation pairing emerging talent with senior advisors on alignment research, governance, and strategy projects. Includes mentorship and career support.

entries.name: Cambridge ERA:AI Fellowship
entries.desc: 10-week, paid research fellowship at the University of Cambridge for researchers and entrepreneurs working on AI safety.

entries.name: Center for Human-Compatible AI (CHAI): Internship
entries.desc: Designed for students and professionals who are interested in research in human-compatible AI. Interns work on a research project supervised by a mentor.

entries.name: Center on Long-Term Risk (CLR): Fellowship
entries.desc: 8-week summer research fellowship with mentorship in London working on challenging research questions relevant to reducing suffering in the long-term future.

entries.name: Effective Thesis Fellowship
entries.desc: Pairs students and early-career researchers with partner organizations working on problems like AI safety. Participants develop a thesis or research project with mentorship.

entries.name: Global Challenges Project (GCP)
entries.desc: Intensive 3-day workshops for people to explore the foundational arguments around risks from advanced AI (and biotechnology). Run by Kairos.

entries.name: GovAI Fellowship
entries.desc: 3-month program by the Centre for the Governance of AI, designed to help professionals transition to working on AI governance – including in roles in which research is not the main duty.

entries.name: Human-aligned AI Summer School
entries.desc: Annual 4-day program held in Prague, Czech Republic, teaching alignment research methodology through talks, workshops, and discussions.

entries.name: Institute for Law & AI (LawAI): Research Fellowships
entries.desc: Paid placements for law students, professionals, and academics to work at the frontier of AI law and policy. Cohorts run across US Law, EU Law, and Legal Frontiers tracks.

entries.name: London AI Safety Research (LASR) Labs
entries.desc: 3-month program where participants work in teams of 3–4, supervised by an experienced AI safety researcher, to write an academic-style paper.

entries.name: Mentorship for Alignment Research Students (MARS)
entries.desc: Part-time research program run by Cambridge AI Safety Hub (CAISH), connecting aspiring researchers with experienced mentors to conduct AI safety research for 2–3 months.

entries.name: ML4Good
entries.desc: 8-day intensive in-person bootcamps upskilling participants in either technical safety research or governance and strategy. Held in various locations around the world.

entries.name: Pivotal Research Fellowship
entries.desc: 15-week program designed to enable promising researchers to produce impactful research and accelerate their careers in AI safety.

entries.name: Talos Fellowship
entries.desc: 7-month program for graduates to launch EU policy careers reducing risks from AI. Comprised of an online reading group, a Brussels policymaking summit, and optional paid placement.

entries.name: Kairos
entries.desc: Fieldbuilding org accelerating talent into AI safety through SPAR (mentored research), Pathfinder (uni group support), GCP (workshops), and the Generator Residency.

entries.name: Cambridge Boston Alignment Initiative (CBAI)
entries.desc: Runs educational programs, conducts and supports research, and disseminates findings to experts and the public.

entries.name: AI In Context
entries.desc: Channel produced by 80,000 Hours presenting thoroughly researched, cinematic stories about what's happening in AI and where the trends are taking us.

entries.name: Doom Debates
entries.desc: Channel hosted by Liron Shapira featuring debates, explainers, and live Q&A sessions, focused on existential risk and other implications of superintelligence.

entries.name: Siliconversations
entries.desc: YouTube channel explaining (mostly) AI safety concepts through entertaining stickman videos.

entries.name: Species
entries.desc: Channel run by Drew Spartz educating a general audience about AI risk through high-effort mini-documentaries.

entries.name: AI Safety Awareness Project (AISAP)
entries.desc: Raising awareness about modern AI, highlighting its benefits and risks, and letting the public know how they can help – mainly through workshops.

entries.name: Collective Action for Existential Safety (CAES)
entries.desc: Aiming to catalyze collective effort towards reducing existential risk, including through an extensive action list for individuals, organizations, and nations.

entries.name: Evitable
entries.desc: Nonprofit founded by David Krueger aiming to inform and organize the public around societal-scale risks and harms of AI.

entries.name: Explainable
entries.desc: Empowering organizations, researchers, and creators to translate the future of AI into stories the world understands.

entries.name: Global AI Moratorium (GAIM)
entries.desc: Calling on policymakers to implement a global moratorium on large AI training runs until alignment is solved.

entries.name: Humans in Control
entries.desc: Advocacy org demanding transparency, accountability, and safeguards to protect humanity from the risks of unchecked AI.

entries.name: Legal Advocates for Safe Science and Technology (LASST)
entries.desc: Researching ways to use legal advocacy to make science and technology safer, informing legal professionals about how to help, and advocating in the courts and policy-setting institutions.

entries.name: Legal Safety Lab
entries.desc: Using legal advocacy in Europe to address risks from frontier technologies, working to foster responsible development and implementation practices.

entries.name: Stop AI
entries.desc: Non-violent civil resistance organization working to permanently ban the development of smarter-than-human AI.

entries.name: The Alliance for Secure AI Action
entries.desc: Communications nonprofit focused on changing the narrative air that policymakers in Washington D.C. breathe with respect to AI safety.

entries.name: The Midas Project (TMP)
entries.desc: Watchdog nonprofit monitoring tech companies, countering corporate propaganda, raising awareness about corner-cutting, and advocating for the responsible development of AI.

entries.name: Torchbearer Community (TBC)
entries.desc: Grassroots advocacy group contacting legislators and leaders to raise awareness about AI safety and urge them to promote and adopt policies that will help humanity thrive.

entries.name: Buddhism & AI Initiative
entries.desc: A collaborative effort to bring together Buddhist communities, technologists, and contemplative researchers worldwide to help shape the future of AI.

entries.name: AI Safety Foundation
entries.desc: Conducting educational initiatives, research support, and public awareness campaigns. Partners with Geoffrey Hinton.

entries.name: AI Policy Bulletin
entries.desc: Publishes policy-relevant perspectives on frontier AI governance, including research summaries, opinions, interviews, and explainers.

entries.name: AI Prospects
entries.desc: Blog by Eric Drexler on AI prospects and their surprising implications for technology, economics, environmental concerns, and military affairs.

entries.name: Bounded Regret
entries.desc: Blog on AI safety by Jacob Steinhardt, a UC Berkeley statistics professor, analyzing risks, forecasting future breakthroughs, and discussing alignment strategies.

entries.name: ChinaTalk
entries.desc: Deep, thoughtful coverage on China, technology, and US-China relations – run by Jordan Schneider.

entries.name: Cold Takes
entries.desc: Blog about transformative AI, futurism, research, ethics, philanthropy etc. by Holden Karnofsky. Includes the "most important century" post series. Last posted in 2024.

entries.name: DeepMind Safety Research

entries.desc: Supported individuals in London interested in working on AI safety by raising awareness of the risks and providing high-quality resources and support.

entries.name: Stop AGI
entries.desc: Website communicating the risks of god-like AI to the public and offering proposals on preventing its development.

entries.name: Superlinear Prizes
entries.desc: Decentralized bounty platform for existential risk reduction and other effective altruist cause areas.

entries.name: WhiteBox Research
entries.desc: Filipino nonprofit aiming to develop more AI interpretability and safety researchers in and around Southeast Asia. Last program was in 2025.

entries.name: OpenAI Foundation: AI Resilience grants
entries.desc: The grant programme of the foundation that controls OpenAI, covering biosecurity, cybersecurity, AI model safety and the effect of AI on young people. On 1 June 2026 the foundation said it was finalising more than USD 130m in grants and would publish the recipients later.

entries.name: OpenAI Superalignment Fast Grants

src.title: OpenAI: Superalignment Fast Grants

src.title: OpenAI: Cybersecurity Grant Program

entries.name: OpenAI Safety Fellowship
